Extending retry conditions now keeps the numeric limit[1]

01Summary

Goal

Keep a numeric retry limit when an extended instance adds detailed retry conditions.[2]

AS-IS

Adding object conditions replaced the parent's numeric retry limit.[1]

TO-BE

A root numeric retry value becomes a limit field before the child conditions are merged.[1]

Impact

The extended instance keeps the requested retry count and the added conditions.[3]

Review result

  • Verification needed Medium

    Confirm the full retry suite

Review limits

  • The example cannot claim that the complete retry suite passes.

02Behavior change

Core change

  • A retry limit of 3 still produces four total attempts after methods are added.[4]

  • Nested request data with a retry key keeps ordinary object merging.[5][6]

Conditions and flow

The special preservation rule applies only when a root numeric retry value meets child object conditions.[1]

  1. The parent sets retry as a number.[7]

  2. The child adds detailed retry conditions as an object.[7]

  3. The root merge expands the number into a limit and then merges the child object.[1]

This model simplifies

The model shows retry forms and the resulting limit, not the full request lifecycle.

This model leaves out

Backoff, hooks, network failures, and method-specific retry decisions.

Check understanding

If the retry limit is 3 and every attempt times out, how many requests run in total?
Show answer and evidence

Four. The limit counts retries after the first request.[4]

04Evidence and scope

Implementation details

  1. Separate root and recursive merging

    Pass root state through the internal merge function.[10][11]

  2. Expand numeric retry shorthand

    Convert the existing number to a limit field before merging child conditions.[12]

  3. Cover request count and nested data

    Focused tests check four attempts and preserve a nested retry key as request data.[4][6]

  2. [2]
    pull request description 3–5 
    `retry` accepts a number as shorthand for `{limit: number}` (per the docs: *"If `retry` is a number, it will be used as `limit` and other defaults will remain in place."*).

However, when a numeric `retry` is set on a parent instance and then extended with an **object**, the numeric limit is silently dropped and falls back to the default (`2`):
  3. [3]
    pull request description 24–26 
    ### Fix

Expand the numeric `retry` shorthand to `{limit: number}` before the deep merge, so extending it with an object preserves the limit. This mirrors the documented shorthand semantics and leaves every other case (object → object, object → number replacement, `replaceOption`) unchanged.

    test/retry.ts · change excerpt 24–35 
    +test('retry - shorthand expansion does not rewrite nested user data with a `retry` key', async t => {
+	const server = await createHttpTestServer(t);
+	server.post('/', (request, response) => {
+		response.json({body: request.body});
+	});
+
+	// A `retry` key inside the `json` body is user data, not the `retry` option,
+	// so the number-to-`{limit}` shorthand must not touch it.
+	const client = ky.create({json: {retry: 3}}).extend({json: {retry: {foo: 'bar'}}});
+
+	const {body} = await client.post(server.url).json<{body: {retry: unknown}}>();
+	t.deepEqual(body.retry, {foo: 'bar'});
